-86.80470,33.50600.name: University of Alabama at Birmingham, Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility
-86.80470,33.50600.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Deidre D. Gunn, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-85.66786,42.96324.name: Van Andel Research Institute
-85.66786,42.96324.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Van Andel Institute. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.18519,52.93714.name: Future Health Biobank
-1.18519,52.93714.state: Nottingham Science Park, Unit 10 -12 Faraday Building, University Boulevard Nottingham, Nottinghamshire, NG7 2QP
-1.18519,52.93714.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.
